title: System degraded
shortDescription: One or more drives in the storage pool have failed, leaving redundancy compromised.
fullDescription:
Synology DSM reports Degraded when a RAID set loses a disk but data is still accessible via remaining parity. The array continues to function but a second failure could cause data loss.

Replace failed drive ASAP. DSM will start rebuild automatically once new disk is inserted.

Monitor SMART status and backup critical data before rebuild completes.

fixSteps.title: Identify failed drive
fixSteps.instruction: Storage Manager > HDD/SSD will show failed drive slot.

fixSteps.title: Backup data
fixSteps.instruction: Run Hyper Backup to ensure offsite copy before rebuild.

fixSteps.title: Replace drive
fixSteps.instruction: Power off (or hot-swap if supported), remove failed drive, insert new compatible drive.

fixSteps.title: Start rebuild
fixSteps.instruction: Storage Manager will prompt to Repair pool; confirm and allow rebuild.

whenToCallPro: If multiple drives fail or rebuild fails, contact Synology support to avoid data loss.

faq.a: Yes but avoid heavy use until rebuild completes.

title: Volume crashed
shortDescription: A storage volume has failed and is no longer accessible.
fullDescription:
A crashed volume means too many drives failed, or the filesystem is corrupt beyond auto-recovery.

Do not write more data. Attempt filesystem check via DSM. If unsuccessful, data recovery may be needed.

Restore from backup is the safest path.

causes.cause: Multiple drive failures exceeding RAID tolerance

fixSteps.title: Do not reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Avoid further writes or power cycling.

fixSteps.title: Check SMART on all disks
fixSteps.instruction: Storage Manager to identify failed disks.

fixSteps.title: Filesystem check
fixSteps.instruction: Storage Manager > Volume > Data Scrubbing / File System Check.

fixSteps.title: Restore from backup
fixSteps.instruction: If volume unrecoverable, create new and restore Hyper Backup.

whenToCallPro: Contact Synology or data recovery service for critical data without backup.

faq.a: Often recoverable via filesystem check or professional service.
Yes to create new volume, but old data needs recovery first.

title: SMART warning
shortDescription: Drive SMART attributes indicate impending failure.
fullDescription:
DSM monitors SMART attributes like reallocated sectors, pending sectors, and uncorrectable errors. Warnings indicate disk is wearing and should be replaced.

Do not ignore — drive will likely fail soon. Back up and swap.

fixSteps.title: Replace drive
fixSteps.instruction: Swap with NAS-grade drive and let RAID rebuild.

title: Fan failed
shortDescription: System cooling fan has stopped or is running incorrectly.
fullDescription:
Dust accumulation, bearing wear, or cable disconnection stops fan. Temperature will rise, risking drive and board damage.

Replace with matching Synology or compatible fan. DSM will alarm continuously until cleared.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Compressed air cleaning; if bearings worn, replace with compatible 92mm or 120mm fan.

whenToCallPro: If warranty active, don't open; contact Synology.

faq.a: Match size and connector; 4-pin PWM preferred.

title: Power supply failure
shortDescription: Internal or redundant PSU has failed.
fullDescription:
Rackmount RS models have dual PSUs with redundancy; DS models have single internal. A PSU failure causes shutdown or alarm.

Replace with identical part number; RS models support hot-swap.

fixSteps.title: Identify failed PSU
fixSteps.instruction: DSM > Info Center > Hardware shows PSU status.

fixSteps.title: Swap PSU
fixSteps.instruction: For rackmount hot-swap; for desktop open case and replace.

whenToCallPro: Desktop models with internal PSU — send to Synology under warranty.

title: Temperature too high
shortDescription: System or drive temperature exceeds safe threshold.
fullDescription:
DSM logs show drive or CPU temperatures over limits (55-60C drives, 70C CPU). Caused by dust, fan failure, ambient heat, or enclosed space.

Clean vents, improve airflow, and replace fans as needed.

fixSteps.title: Check placement
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure 10cm clearance all sides; not in cabinet.

fixSteps.title: Clean vents and fans
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, use compressed air to clean.

fixSteps.title: Check fan operation
fixSteps.instruction: Verify fan spins and replace if dead.

fixSteps.title: Adjust fan mode
fixSteps.instruction: DSM > Hardware & Power > Fan Speed Mode > Full Speed if needed.

whenToCallPro: If shutdown persists despite clean NAS, hardware service needed.

title: Network connection lost
shortDescription: Ethernet link dropped or not established.
fullDescription:
Cable, switch, or NIC issues break network. DSM shows port down. Link link aggregation or failover can mask single port issues.

Check cable, switch port, and NIC settings.

fixSteps.title: Test cable
fixSteps.instruction: Try known-good cable and different switch port.

fixSteps.title: Reset DSM network
fixSteps.instruction: Control Panel > Network > Network Interface > reset to DHCP.

whenToCallPro: If NIC chip fried, hardware service needed.
videoSearchQuery: Synology NAS network connection lost fix

faq.q: Can I reset DSM network via console?
faq.a: Yes by pressing reset button briefly for network reset.

title: Backup job failed
shortDescription: Scheduled Hyper Backup or similar job could not complete.
fullDescription:
Common failure causes: destination full, network drop, permission error, or source file issue. DSM log details specific error.

Review Hyper Backup log, fix cause, re-run.

fixSteps.title: Review log
fixSteps.instruction: Open Hyper Backup > Log Center for error details.

fixSteps.title: Verify credentials
fixSteps.instruction: Re-enter cloud provider credentials if expired.

faq.a: No; only the new snapshot failed.

title: DSM update error
shortDescription: DSM system update failed or did not reboot cleanly.
fullDescription:
DSM upgrades occasionally fail due to package conflicts, insufficient space, or corrupted download.

Retry from Control Panel; manual PAT file install possible. Recovery mode may be needed.

fixSteps.title: Download PAT manually
fixSteps.instruction: Get PAT file from Synology Download Center.

fixSteps.title: Manual install
fixSteps.instruction: Control Panel > Manual DSM Update > upload PAT.

fixSteps.title: Recovery mode
fixSteps.instruction: If bricked, use Synology Assistant to recover.

whenToCallPro: If data loss risk, Synology support.

faq.a: Normally no; DSM and data are separate.

title: RAID rebuild failed
shortDescription: Array failed to complete rebuild after drive replacement.
fullDescription:
Rebuild can fail if another drive has bad sectors or replacement drive is faulty. May leave volume crashed.

Check SMART on all drives, scrub if possible, consider professional data recovery.
whenToCallPro: Critical data at risk — Synology or recovery specialist.

faq.a: Built for 24/7 vibration tolerance and TLER.

title: Drive removed unexpectedly
shortDescription: A drive has been ejected or lost connection.
fullDescription: Could be unintentional (loose tray) or hardware failure. Check tray seating and cable; SMART the drive after reseat.

faq.a: Yes; DSM will re-add if healthy.

title: Memory error
shortDescription: RAM test or ECC reports errors.
fullDescription:
Bad RAM causes crashes, data corruption, and package errors. DSM provides Memory Test under Control Panel > Info Center.

Replace with Synology-validated RAM.

fixSteps.title: Reseat RAM
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, open RAM door, reinsert modules.

faq.a: Validated brands work but Synology branded avoids support issues.

title: SHR conversion failed
shortDescription: Storage pool expansion or SHR conversion did not complete.
fullDescription:
SHR (Synology Hybrid RAID) expansion can fail if drive sizes are wrong, one drive has errors, or operation interrupted.

Check logs and drive health before retry.

fixSteps.title: Retry conversion
fixSteps.instruction: Storage Manager > Action > Repair or Expand.

title: Package corrupted
shortDescription: A DSM package cannot start due to corruption.
fullDescription: Package Center reports a package as damaged. Usually reinstall fixes. Sometimes clean removal and reinstall needed.

faq.a: Package Center preserves config when available.

title: License expired
shortDescription: Surveillance Station or other paid license expired or invalid.
fullDescription:
Synology offers free bundled licenses plus paid add-ons (Surveillance Station cameras, Active Backup). Expired or invalid licenses disable features.

Reactivate or purchase new license via Synology account.
